titleEn: Tub vs. Walk-in Shower Renovation in Vancouver: What to Consider in 2026
titleZh: 温哥华浴缸与步入式淋浴改造：2026年需要考虑什么
contentEn:
If you are deciding between keeping a bathtub or installing a walk-in shower in your Vancouver home, the short answer is this: a walk-in shower delivers better long-term value for most Vancouver homeowners, particularly in condos and townhouses where aging in place and resale appeal both matter. The City of Vancouver building code requires at least one bathtub or shower per dwelling unit, so either choice is legally acceptable.

聚星裝修 has completed over 58 renovation projects across Metro Vancouver. This guide compares the two options across cost, code requirements, accessibility and resale value, so you can make the right choice for your home and your budget.

How Much Does a Tub-to-Shower Conversion Cost in Vancouver in 2026?

A standard tub-to-walk-in-shower conversion in Vancouver typically ranges from $4,500 to $13,000, depending on materials, plumbing modifications and whether you are working in a Strata-titled building. A new alcove bathtub installation runs $3,800 to $9,500 including labour and permit fees. Vancouver building permit fees for bathroom alterations start at $150 and scale with project value; a plumbing permit adds approximately $150 more. Strata approval, required in most Metro Vancouver condo and townhouse complexes, typically takes two to four weeks to obtain.

ScopeTypical Range (CAD)
Tub-to-walk-in shower conversion$4,500 - $13,000
New alcove bathtub install$3,800 - $9,500
Vancouver building permit (bathroom alt.)$150 - $300
Strata approval (condo/townhouse)2-4 weeks processing

These figures are based on 2025-2026 publicly available contractor estimates and City of Vancouver permit fee schedules. Actual costs vary based on site conditions, material selections and building age.

What Vancouver Building Code Requires

Vancouver's Building By-law (Chapter 64) requires at least one functioning bathtub OR shower in every residential dwelling unit. If you remove the last tub in a home with only one bathroom, you must install a shower to remain compliant. You do not need to keep a bathtub if a shower is present. Removing a bathtub in a two-bathroom home is unrestricted as long as one bathing fixture remains. Any bathroom renovation involving plumbing work requires a plumbing permit from the City of Vancouver, and a building permit may also be required if structural or layout changes are involved.

Accessibility: Aging in Place

A walk-in shower with a low or zero threshold is the better choice if anyone in the home is over 65 or has mobility limitations. Step-over bathtubs require a 17-25 cm raise of the leg, which is a documented fall risk for seniors. A zero-threshold walk-in shower eliminates that barrier entirely. Universal design guidelines published by the National Research Council of Canada note that curbless showers reduce fall risk in bathrooms by up to 33 percent for residents over 65. Vancouver's Seniors' Advocate has published resources noting that home modifications enabling aging in place can delay or eliminate the need for assisted living.

If you have young children, a bathtub is still practical, but you can install a built-in bench seat inside a walk-in shower to serve both needs.

Resale Value in Metro Vancouver

In Metro Vancouver's resale market, the impact depends on your home type. For single-family homes, removing the only bathtub in a two-plus bathroom home can reduce buyer interest, particularly among families. For condos and townhouses in areas like Richmond, Burnaby and Surrey, buyers frequently view a modern walk-in shower as a premium feature rather than a drawback. A 2024 analysis by the Canadian Real Estate Association noted that updated bathrooms ranked among the top three features driving buyer interest in Metro Vancouver. Overbuilding showers in a neighbourhood of predominantly family homes (east Vancouver, Port Moody) can slightly reduce appeal; underbuilding in a primarily retirement-oriented building can reduce marketability.

Which Should You Choose?

Choose a walk-in shower if: you live in a condo or townhouse, you are renovating for aging in place, you want lower maintenance, or your second bathroom already has a tub. Choose a bathtub if: you have young children, your home has only one bathroom and is in a family-oriented neighbourhood, or you plan to sell within two years and comparable homes in your area all have tubs.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I remove my bathtub and replace it with just a shower in Vancouver?

Yes, as long as at least one bathing fixture (bathtub or shower) remains in the home. If it is your only bathroom, you must install a shower to comply with Vancouver's building by-law.

Do I need a permit to convert a bathtub to a walk-in shower in Vancouver?

Yes. Any work that modifies plumbing requires a plumbing permit from the City of Vancouver. If structural changes, floor layout modifications or changes to exterior walls are involved, a building permit is also required. Permit fees typically start at $150 for plumbing.

How long does a tub-to-shower conversion take in Vancouver?

A standard conversion typically takes two to three weeks from permit approval to completion. Strata approval for condo and townhouse renovations can add two to four weeks before work begins. 聚星裝修 manages the permit and strata process as part of every full bathroom renovation.

Will removing my bathtub reduce my home's resale value in Vancouver?

It depends on the neighbourhood and buyer profile. In condo and townhouse markets, a modern walk-in shower often has neutral or positive resale impact. In single-family home neighbourhoods with family buyers, removing the only tub in a multi-bathroom home can reduce appeal. 聚星裝修 can advise on your specific neighbourhood before you decide.

Yes. Our team manages the full strata approval process, permit applications and inspection coordination for every project in Metro Vancouver strata buildings.

2026年温哥华将浴缸改为淋浴需要多少钱？

温哥华标准的浴缸转步入式淋浴改造通常在 $4,500 至 $13,000 加元之间，具体取决于材料、管道修改以及您是否在分契式建筑中施工。新建嵌入式浴缸安装包括人工和许可费在内，运行 $3,800 至 $9,500 加元。温哥华建筑许可证费用从 $150 起，并根据项目价值递增；管道许可证另外增加约 $150。大多数 Metro Vancouver 公寓和联排别墅综合体需要分契审批，通常需要两到四周才能获得。

范围典型价格（加元）
浴缸转步入式淋浴改造$4,500 - $13,000
新建嵌入式浴缸安装$3,800 - $9,500

这些数字基于 2025-2026 年公开可用的承包商估算和温哥华市政府许可证费用表。实际成本因现场条件、材料选择和建筑年份而异。

温哥华建筑法规要求

温哥华建筑条例（ 第64章）要求每个住宅单元至少配备一个正常运作的浴缸或淋浴设施。如果您拆除家中唯一浴室的最后一个浴缸，则必须安装淋浴以保持合规。如果已有淋浴，则无需保留浴缸。两浴室以上的住宅中，拆除浴缸不受限制，只要仍保留一个沐浴设施即可。任何涉及管道工程的浴室装修都需要获得温哥华市政府的管道许可证，如果涉及结构或布局变更，可能还需要建筑许可证。

无障碍性：安享晚年

如果您家中有人年满65岁或行动不便，低门槛或无门槛步入式淋浴是更好的选择。跨浴缸需要抬高腿17-25厘米，这是老年人已记录的跌倒风险。无门槛步入式淋浴完全消除了这一障碍。加拿大国家研究委员会发布的通用设计指南指出，无门槛淋浴可将65岁以上居民的浴室跌倒风险降低多达33%。温哥华长者维权人士发布的资源指出，使人们能够安享晚年的家庭装修可以延缓或消除对辅助生活的需求。

如果您有幼儿，浴缸仍然实用，但您可以在步入式淋浴内安装嵌入式座椅来满足两种需求。

Metro Vancouver 的转售价值

在 Metro Vancouver 的转售市场中，影响取决于您的房屋类型。对于独立屋来说，拆除两套以上浴室中唯一的浴缸可能会降低买家兴趣，特别是对有家庭的买家。在列治文、本拿比和素里等地区的公寓和联排别墅中，购房者经常将现代步入式淋浴视为高端设施，而不是缺点。加拿大房地产协会2024年的分析指出，翻新的浴室是 Metro Vancouver 购房者兴趣的前三大因素之一。在以家庭为主的社区过度安装淋浴可能会略微降低吸引力；在以退休为主的建筑中安装不足则可能降低市场竞争力。

您应该选择哪个？

如果您属于以下情况，请选择步入式淋浴：您住在公寓或联排别墅中、为了安享晚年而装修、想要减少维护工作，或者您的第二间浴室已有浴缸。如果属于以下情况，请选择浴缸：您有幼儿、您的房屋只有一间浴室且位于以家庭为主的社区，或者您计划在两年内出售房屋且该地区同类房屋都有浴缸。

常见问题

在温哥华，我可以拆除浴缸并仅用淋浴替代吗？

可以，只要家中至少保留一个沐浴设施（浴缸或淋浴）。如果这是您唯一的浴室，则必须安装淋浴以符合温哥华建筑条例。

在温哥华，将浴缸改为淋浴需要许可证吗？

需要。任何修改管道的工程都需要获得温哥华市政府的管道许可证。如果涉及结构变更、楼层布局修改或外墙变更，则还需要建筑许可证。管道许可证费用通常从 $150 起。

在温哥华，浴缸转淋浴改造需要多长时间？

标准改造通常需要两到三周才能完成，从许可证批准到竣工。公寓和联排别墅装修的分契审批可在工程开始前增加两到四周。聚星装修在每个完整浴室装修项目中都会管理许可证和分契流程。

拆除浴缸会降低我在温哥华的房屋转售价值吗？

这取决于社区和买家情况。在公寓和联排别墅市场中，现代步入式淋浴通常具有中性或正面转售影响。在有家庭买家的独立屋社区中，拆除多浴室房屋中唯一的浴缸可能会降低吸引力。聚星装修可以在您决定之前就您的特定社区提供建议。
